newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison to release record results.
newsitem.headline: Morrison to release record results.

text.p: Morrison Petroleums Ltd, target of a C$652 million hostile takeover bid from Canadian 88 Energy Corp, said on Tuesday it expected to report record financial and operating results this week.
"We'll be releasing the financial and operating results relating to 1996 this week," Morrison vice-president of finance Paul Charron said in a phone interview.
Asked if the results, which will be announced earlier than planned because of the takeover offer, would be record results, Charron said: "Yes."

He also said the company expected its board of directors to recommend to shareholders whether to reject or accept the bid on Monday, although several industry sources have said they expected Morrison to fight the advance.
Morrison chairman Gordon Stollery said last week he would be "shocked" if the company's financial did not deem the bid as too cheap.
Canadian 88 last week offered C$10 cash, to a maximum of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
The offer is contingent on Morrison waiving its new shareholder rights plan, which would extend the time to consider the bid to 60 from the standard 21 days.
Morrison's poison pill was announced two days before the bid, in a move Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval said he believed was in anticipation of the offer.
"We're not sure we understand why he's objecting to our shareholder rights plan, considering he has one of his own," Charron said. "He does have one with a similar 60-day provision."
At stake in the battle are potentially rich natural gas reserves in the southwestern Alberta foothills, where Morrison is a large acreage owner.
Morrison shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange closed on Tuesday down 0.15 to 10.15. Canadian 88 was down 0.20 to 6.60.
